Green Villa with Good Food
Mar 2019
Trois Gourmands is a famous French restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City. The restaurant is a big villa with a swimming pool. Its green walls make it very distinctive in the residential zone. There are outdoor tables and a big grill in the garden area. The interior is beautifully decorated with fresh orchids, fancy curtains and colourful paintings. Ambience is great! The main dining room and private rooms are spacious, bright and well furnished with carpets, air conditioning, and comfortable chairs. Servers and chefs are all very friendly and accommodating. They even accept new US dollar bills. Depending on your choice of entrées, set lunch can cost around VND 1,046,000 (or USD 45) to VND 2,379,000 (or USD 103), which is quite expensive in Vietnamese standards. Highly recommend the flavorful “Nem de Foie Gras” (Goose Liver Spring Roll), the refreshing “Tartare de crab” (Crab Tartare), and “Profiteroles au Chocolat” (Chocolate "Profiteroles" with Vanilla ice cream). One thing that needs improvement though is the slow serving speed; taking more than 3 hours to enjoy a 5-course French lunch is a bit too long.

Fine Western Food in Saigon (HCM City)
Oct 2019
This restaurant is in a house (mansion) with a yard and a pool, which apparently was a home before, and subsequently a restaurant (before it became the current Trois Gourmands restaurant). 

Seating may be indoors or al fresco. We arrived on an evening that was partly showery but sat outside anyway, with no unpleasant effects as there was no rain when we had dinner (note nevertheless than Saigon/HCM City is a place where it does sometimes rain). 

The service is very good and the staff were knowledgable and friendly. 

The menu was not huge but offered acceptable choices. We were two of us and we ordered a sampling of food which we shared. It was good but not unforgettable. The pricing was fine dining pricing by Indochinese standards, but not exorbitant.

This place may be recommended for a family or a group of friends out, because of the good service and the acceptably comfortable seating.

It is nevertheless not in the heart of town and even the taxi driver had to look for the location. It is not an impossible address to find, partly because the restaurant is located in an area with a handful of other fine restaurants. Nevertheless bear in mind it is not in the usual heard-of-town type of high-grade location; it is a small distance out, in an acceptable neighbourhood.

DIsappointing
Oct 2019
We were recommended this restaurant by a friend as a place with good affordable French food in HCM. Based on this, we ventured out to District 2 (quite a distance from District 1 hotel where we were staying) for a girls night out. We arrived at an old school colonial looking bungalow and stepped inside. Despite having made a reservation, they had to arrange a table for us clearly having failed in preparing one for us based on the earlier reservation. We all took the 5 course set menu at USD45 per person. We started with truffle scrambled egg which was good (not the best we have had) followed by a palate cleanser. 2 of my friends chose the scallop with asparagus appetizer and was surprised to find no asparagus in their dishes when it arrived. Puzzled, they asked the waiter who was confused then said he would check with the kitchen. He came back with the response that they had run out of asparagus !! Whilst these things happen, you should either tell the wait staff that this dish is no longer available or if you are replacing it with some other vegetables in this case,you should inform the customers and not stay silent as if the customers are idiots who can't tell the difference between asparagus and beans which was put on the plate to replace the asparagus. The rest of the dishes were ranged from blah to bad. Our sou vide lamb was so tough & dry (which I thought was impossible with sou vide) and both of us girls who ordered it probably ate about 1/3 of the dish only. Only 1 winner of the various courses that night ix the white fish ravioli with white wine sauce. The cheese platter was generous and the homemade soft cheeses were good. Desserts were OK at best. Whilst it wasn't expensive for French food, the standard of food to us was mediocre and the service was friendly but not particularly of good standard. The place was busy so obviously they are popular although our party could not really understand why based on our dinner that night. Having had so many good meals in HCM (eg. An Vien, Vietnam House, Propaganda Cafe & 4Ps), we would not recommend going to this restaurant.

Amazing French Lunch at Ho Chi Minh City
Mar 2019 • Family
This was my first visit to Vietnam and one of our family friends highly recommended Trois Gourmands for our large group. We were able to contact the restaurant through email and did not even need to set up a menu (but if time is important to you, setting up a menu is actually a good idea!). For lunch, they basically have four different menus priced from USD$45 to 60 featuring a truffle scrambled egg starter, a starter (the prices varies on the number of starters you want), main course, cheese plate, and dessert. If you want steak or specialty dishes, you just pay a surcharge. Some of us ordered the steak (entrecôte) which has a USD $25 surcharge. The food was basically amazing, The staffs were friendly and tried very hard. There were a little mistakes here and there but given our large party with variety of dishes ordered, it was acceptable. We even got to meet the Chef and visit the kitchen, which is super clean and impressive. I also love the outdoor grill. I just can't say enough good things about this restaurant. I have my best meal in Vietnam here.

Excellence in French cuisine.
Nov 2014 • Family
We visited this restaurant as guests of our son-in-law and daughter who are well versed in the restaurant scene of Ho Chi Minh. They chose this restaurant as an occasion to celebrate our anniversary. What an excellent choice it proved to be. The menu had a wide variety of starter dishes and mains, the mains comprising some 6 fish dishes and at least a dozen other dishes including beef, lamb, chicken, rabbit and veal (kidneys) options. Starter dishes sampled by our party included ris de veal, a foie gras medley, veal tartar, scallops and a seafood ravioli. All were extremely tasteful and innovate lay presented. The same can be said of our main dishes which were braised rabbit in a red wine sauce, rognon de veau, seared lamb back strap and a sea bass ravioli in a white sauce.
One big plus about the restaurant is that it permits patrons to bring their own wines and it does not charge corkage for this privelege, thus elevating the restaurant into a high value for money category. Both outdoors and indoor (air-conditioned) seating is a available. Service was good, especially by the young waitresses who had a good command of the English language and were knowledgable of the dishes and their ingredients. A meal of similar quality and with a similar ambience would be at least twice as costly in Europe or North America.
